To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the pressure for asymmetric nuclear matter is bounded above by the pressure for neutron matter; (2) the pressure for symmetric nuclear matter is bounded below by the pressure for symmetric neutron matter; and (3) the pressure for nuclear matter is bounded between the pressure for asymmetric neutron matter and symmetric neutron matter.

the pressure of nuclear matter is bounded from above by a simple function of the density and the neutron-proton asymmetry and that the pressure of neutron matter is bounded from below by a simple function.

the pressure of asymmetric and pure neutron matter is upper bounded by a function which is linear in the neutron chemical potential, and that the pressure of neutron matter is also upper bounded by a linear function of the neutron density.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following: 1) the derivation of inequalities using lowest-order chiral effective field theory for nuclear matter; and 2) a comparison between these inequalities and the results obtained from a variational Monte Carlo calculation.
inequalities that constrain the pressure of asymmetric matter.
proving inequalities for the pressure of asymmetric and neutron matter using effective field theory for neutrons and protons.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the pressure of asymmetric matter is bounded from above by the pressure of pure neutron matter, and that the pressure of symmetric matter is bounded by the pressure of asymmetric neutron matter.
the pressure of nuclear matter is always larger than the pressure of neutron matter at the same density.
the pressure of neutron matter is less than the pressure of nuclear matter with a proton fraction equal to the neutron fraction of neutron matter, for any density and temperature.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we show that the pressure of neutron matter and asymmetric nuclear matter are bounded from above by that of a system of neutrons and protons interacting via a two-body potential with a repulsive core, which is known to be unbound.
the pressure of asymmetric and neutron matter is bounded by the pressure of symmetric nuclear matter.
we have shown the existence of a maximum pressure for asymmetric nuclear matter and the existence of a minimum pressure for pure neutron matter.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the nuclear symmetry energy is bounded from above by a combination of the nuclear matter pressure and the pressure of pure neutron matter.

the pressure of nuclear and neutron matter is bounded by the pressure of symmetric nuclear matter, and the difference between the pressures of asymmetric nuclear matter with neutron excess and symmetric nuclear matter is bounded by a function of neutron excess and the pressure of symmetric matter.
the pressure of neutron matter is always greater than the pressure of asymmetric matter at the same density and isospin fraction.
